speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned a concerning rash and recent health changes, but I need more details to begin my assessment. Can you describe the appearance, location, and any associated symptoms of the rash, and when did it first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; given the new cough and arthritis management, are you currently taking any new medications or supplements since seeing your primary care provider? Also, does the rash appear on your face or upper torso, and is it accompanied by fever or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Iron Deficiency Anemia is unlikely to cause mucositis and a sudden upper-back rash; this presentation is more consistent with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) triggered by a recent medication for arthritis or cough. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and Medication Review. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body dermatogram.
